summary: Verified real-GPS bug fix in /app/frontend/app/alert.tsx. All 8 code-level checks pass (BestForNavigation used everywhere, warm-up watcher via watchPositionAsync storing latestFixRef, 15s/50m freshness gating in handleImSafe, hasServicesEnabledAsync check with location_services_off, permission_denied path, POST payload shape intact, success toast + auto-nav wired, no hardcoded lat/lng literals). E2E on web preview with geolocation mocked to Mriehel, Malta (35.8916, 14.4658 ±10m): warm fix was consumed (console: '[QuakeGuard] using warm GPS fix → 35.8916 14.4658 ± 10 m'), POST https://safequake.onrender.com/api/status returned HTTP 200, alert-success-toast rendered. However a NEW regression was found: on AlertScreen unmount, sub?.remove() throws 'LocationEventEmitter.removeSubscription is not a function' (web-only expo-location issue) — this triggers a red-screen LogBox overlay and BLOCKS the auto-nav back to Home on web preview.

ui_bugs.issue: sub?.remove() throws 'TypeError: _LocationEventEmitter.LocationEventEmitter.removeSubscription is not a function' on unmount when running on Expo web. This is caused by the newly added watchPositionAsync subscription. Red-screen LogBox overlay appears and the auto-nav back to Home is aborted after 'I'M SAFE'.

react_native_issues.issue: LocationSubscription.remove() is not fully implemented in expo-location web shim for the version used. Recommend wrapping cleanup in try/catch so it's harmless on web and still works on iOS/Android: try { sub?.remove(); } catch {}. Alternatively, only start the watcher when Platform.OS !== 'web'.

action_items: Wrap sub?.remove() cleanup in a try/catch (or gate the warm-up watcher behind Platform.OS !== 'web') to prevent the red-screen and restore auto-nav back to Home on web preview.
No changes needed to the core GPS logic — BestForNavigation + warm-up ref + 15s/50m gating is correctly implemented and produces the real live-location fix in the payload.
critical_code_review_comments: Bug fix implementation is clean: warm-up watcher + ref + freshness gate is a good pattern.
Consider also using an accuracy-improving loop that resolves once accuracy <=20m for even better fixes on cold-start; not required now.
The web-only LocationSubscription.remove crash should be guarded — it is now the only user-visible failure on the web preview flow.

success_rate.frontend: 7/8 checks pass; primary bug (wrong location) fixed, but a new unmount-time exception blocks auto-nav on web

context_for_next_testing_agent: Primary fix verified with mocked geolocation (Playwright context.set_geolocation to Mriehel, Malta). POST to safequake.onrender.com/api/status returns 200 and the payload uses the warm high-accuracy fix. Remaining issue is the expo-location subscription cleanup crash on web — a small try/catch or Platform gate around sub.remove() will fully close this out. On a real device the accuracy of BestForNavigation cannot be validated via web Playwright.
rca_of_issue: RCA of the newly discovered regression: The warm-up useEffect (alert.tsx lines 44-72) subscribes via Location.watchPositionAsync. Its cleanup calls sub?.remove(). Under expo-location's web shim, LocationSubscription.remove() eventually calls LocationEventEmitter.removeSubscription which is not a function on web, causing an uncaught TypeError during React unmount. This surfaces as a red-screen LogBox and prevents router.replace('/') from completing the navigation. Reproduction: open the app on web, tap trigger-alert-btn, tap im-safe-btn, wait ~1.2s for auto-nav — LogBox error appears instead of Home. Mitigation: wrap sub?.remove() in try/catch, or start the watcher only on native (Platform.OS !== 'web'). Root cause is not in the bug fix logic itself — it's a platform-shim gap that the newly-added subscription now exercises.
